summary.text: 牛 is a picture of an ox focused on its head and horns. The graph names the animal; it is also used as a radical. The date of the earliest surviving example is unresolved.

formation.text: Pictographic: the graph depicts an ox’s head and horns. Early oracle-bone and bronze forms are interpreted as frontal views; some bronze forms also show ears, eyes, and nose.

history.text: The transmitted Shuowen description identifies horns, head, and a tail or raised-back feature. Its gloss calls 牛 a large sacrificial animal; later commentary offers a different interpretation based on the animal’s work and patterns. These are historical readings of the graph and word, not independent proof of its origin.

The recorded form classes include oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal forms. The listed specimens are not individually dated here, so they do not establish the earliest surviving example.
牛 is reported both for cattle and in personal names in bronze inscriptions; those examples do not establish when either use began.

uncertainties.text: The head-and-horns pictographic analysis is supported, but the earliest securely dated specimen and the dates of the listed form classes remain unresolved. No competing formation or specific graphic corruption is documented here.
Figurative stubbornness, star-name, zodiac, calendar, and surname uses are listed in a modern dictionary, but their dates and connections to the animal sense are not established.

Supplied local readings give Mandarin niú and Baxter–Sagart Middle Chinese ngjuw and Old Chinese *[ŋ]ʷə. The character-specific Unihan record was inaccessible; these readings do not establish graphic formation, and 牛 is not analyzed as a phonetic component.

senses.text: The graph is interpreted as depicting the animal, and 牛 is reported in an inscription referring to cattle. The earliest securely dated occurrence is unresolved, so this is the earliest supported sense, not a dated first use.

senses.period: Shuowen Jiezi; date of use not established here
senses.text: The transmitted Shuowen entry glosses 牛 as a large sacrificial animal. This dictionary gloss does not establish a separate earlier sense or the graph’s original meaning.

limitations.text: No dated corpus of written senses establishes the chronology or semantic connections among the animal, figurative, astronomical, calendar, zodiac, and surname uses.

overview.text: 牛 depicts an ox, focusing on its head and horns, and names the animal. The earliest securely dated written example remains unresolved.
